source.flyway: V1 through V20, applied unmodified to a disposable empty MySQL 8.0 database
source.mongoArchivePolicy: The two observed historical collections have no active Java collection mapping. Preserve every canonical Extended JSON document in native_legacy_mongo without creating current timetable rows. Missing active collections export as empty files; any other unrecognized collection still blocks export.

mysqlMetadataArchive.inventory: Exactly the 165 baseline business tables and both named metadata tables; unknown tables and additional business columns fail closed.
mysqlMetadataArchive.comparison: Only utf8_/utf8mb3_ collation aliases and ASCII-only charset-introduced string literals inside DEFAULT_GENERATED json_array expressions are canonicalized. Non-ASCII, escaped content, ordinary defaults, other expressions and actual schema differences remain exact.
mysqlMetadataArchive.export: Both histories include every row, including failed or historical migrations, and exact SHOW CREATE TABLE JSON. Each file records source row count, byte count and SHA-256; current history must prove successful V20.
mysqlMetadataArchive.destination: 0002_source_metadata_archive.sql adds native_source_metadata_file descriptors and ordered native_source_metadata_chunk base64 payloads. Both JSONL histories, both DDL files and the original snapshot manifest are archived byte-for-byte in 48KiB chunks.
mysqlMetadataArchive.verification: Conversion checks file hashes, row counts, current-history manifest agreement and reconstructed archive hashes. Import re-reads every chunk from D1, checks descriptor/count/order and recomputes original SHA-256 before marking verified.
mysqlMetadataArchive.schemaGeneration: Run node scripts/generate-schema.mjs --schema-only after additive metadata schema changes. Applied migrations 0000 and 0001 remain unchanged.

exportPrerequisites: Node 24, mysql2, mongoexport, mongosh; Wrangler available to import through the workspace dependency
MYSQL_URL and MONGO_DATABASE must select the observed koin schemas; exporter rejects other MySQL/Mongo database names. MONGO_URI and REDIS_URL must point only at the approved koin containers/tunnels.
MYSQL_URL, MONGO_URI, MONGO_DATABASE and REDIS_URL are supplied only at execution and never committed.

Strict writer-quiesced mode requires all Java/API/background writers stopped across MySQL/Mongo/Redis; Redis SCAN is not an atomic snapshot. Explicit per-store online bootstrap is a different, weaker mode with its own provenance and CLI opt-in.
Redis ACL permits SCAN, TYPE, per-type reads, TIME, PTTL, and the included EVAL script containing only TIME/PTTL reads; expiry uses Redis server time, not workstation time
Live Flyway V20 successful and all 165 table names, column types/nullability/defaults/collations/generated expressions, indexes, CHECK constraints and foreign keys match source metadata

Strict-mode source DATETIME offset must be established independently from live JVM/JDBC. For online bootstrap, user explicitly selected +09:00 from the upstream Asia/Seoul Dockerfile despite unobserved running JVM/JDBC settings; this declared assumption is recorded in conversion provenance.

Source MySQL server SYSTEM timezone observed UTC; this does not establish application JVM/JDBC DATETIME interpretation. Upstream Dockerfile declares Asia/Seoul localtime, but actual running JVM flags, TZ and JDBC connection timezone remain unverified.

Owner registration/reset clients must submit the one-time purpose-and-phone-bound verification_token returned by SMS code verification; old clients that omit it are rejected and must be updated before cutover.
S3 source bucket/R2 private destination and file-delivery policy belong to the separate file-migration workflow; they do not block a read-only MySQL pre-extraction or DB-only snapshot preparation.
No application traffic on the newly created D1 target until import manifest verification succeeds

preExtraction.scope: MySQL koin only, read-only consistent transaction; no Mongo/Redis data and no object transfer.
preExtraction.status: Writers may continue; mark quiesced=false and complete=false, keep the output private with restrictive filesystem permissions, and never pass it to the converter/importer or publish it as a three-store snapshot.
preExtraction.promotion: The MySQL-only pre-extraction cannot be promoted directly. Obtain a complete verified MySQL/Mongo/Redis capture in either strict writer-quiesced mode or explicitly approved per-store-online mode; the latter records Mongo/Redis rolling reads and cross-store time gaps without claiming writer quiescence.

onlineBootstrap.authorization: User explicitly approved independent online per-store captures without stopping writers, with MySQL repeatable-read transaction, Mongo sequential collection cursors and Redis SCAN/per-key reads. This is not a cross-store point-in-time snapshot; Mongo updates and Redis keys can change during their own scans.
onlineBootstrap.manifest: Require complete=true only after all expected source files, inventories, counts and SHA-256/byte descriptors exist; quiesced=false, captureMode=per-store-online, consistency=per-store-online, storeCaptures.mysql/mongo/redis UTC start/end and per-store consistency labels, plus pre/post Mongo inventories and Redis server TIME. Unknown collections/schema/keys and corrupted/missing files remain fatal.
onlineBootstrap.converter: Use `node scripts/convert-snapshot.mjs SNAPSHOT NEW_CONVERTED +09:00 --allow-online-bootstrap`; +09:00 is explicitly operator-declared from upstream Dockerfile, NOT verified running JVM/JDBC. Preserve calendar exceptions and UTC MySQL TIMESTAMP handling. Validate FK/integrity/counts and fail on cross-store conflicts rather than silently dropping records.
onlineBootstrap.import: Use `node scripts/import-d1.mjs CONVERTED NEW_ISOLATED_D1 --local|--remote --allow-online-bootstrap` only after validated conversion and point-risk approval. Import production and Preview into distinct fresh inactive D1 targets from the same complete original snapshot; verify full counts, metadata hashes, FK/integrity and provenance before binding activation. No source overwrite or shared Preview/production auth authority.
onlineBootstrap.strictMode: Existing --sources-quiesced export and unflagged converter/importer remain strict; neither incomplete MySQL pre-extraction nor an unflagged online manifest is importable.

representations.int: INTEGER with integer storage class and exact signed/unsigned source ranges; ordinary IDs remain JavaScript numbers
representations.bigint: Canonical signed 64-bit decimal TEXT, checked through exact SQLite CAST roundtrip; numeric predicates and ordering require CAST(column AS INTEGER), IDs are never coerced through JavaScript Number
representations.bigintAutoIncrement: notification and notification_subscribe use native_sequence, allocated by allocateBigintId and initialized to imported maximum; gaps on failed business operations are allowed as in MySQL
representations.decimal: Exact decimal TEXT; exporter refuses numeric JSON conversion, scale and range checked
representations.binary16: Canonical lowercase UUID TEXT, exact 16-byte binary conversion
representations.binaryOther: BLOB/Uint8Array, base64 in export envelopes and hex SQL literals
representations.json: Original MySQL JSON text retained byte-for-byte after syntax validation; JSON_VALID enforced; Drizzle JSON mapping is used only for actual source JSON columns
representations.timestamp: UTC SQL datetime text; fractional source digits preserved
representations.datetime: Declared source timezone shifted to UTC SQL text, except new_koreatech_articles.registered_at, which is a LocalDate calendar value
representations.mongoDatetime: ISO UTC for chat instants; citybus_timetables.updated_at preserves source local calendar display semantics
representations.nativeExpiry: Owner-defined SQL UTC/ISO UTC text or integer epoch milliseconds, encoded explicitly by native-schema.mjs
representations.onUpdate: SQLite AFTER UPDATE triggers update source ON UPDATE columns only when other values change and timestamp value is unchanged; SQLite cannot distinguish explicitly reassigning the same old timestamp from omitting that column

collation.sql: Source *_ci columns use actual SQLite NOCASE in both DDL and Drizzle custom types; this supports only ASCII folding, not arbitrary MySQL Unicode equality
collation.storage: native_collation_key has PRIMARY KEY(scope,owner) and UNIQUE(scope,normalized). Original display text stays unchanged. Converter populates every applicable source unique index. Runtime normalizedUniqueWrites must be in the same atomic batch as writes; normalizedUniqueLookup queries the registry
collation.normalization: PAD SPACE for non0900 collations; general_ci uses NFD, other *_ci uses NFKD; lowercase plus combining-mark removal; final-sigma folding; general_ci sharp-s to s, Unicode sharp-s to ss; oe-ligature folding outside general_ci; ae/stroked-l/stroked-d/slashed-o folding only for0900
collation.limits: This is an explicit approximation, not MySQL UCA4/UCA9/general_ci weight tables. Context-sensitive contractions, all-script case/mark equivalences, compatibility characters and utf8mb3 supplementary-character restrictions are not fully reproduced. SQL LIKE/equality/sorts remain SQLite semantics unless a domain uses normalized lookup. Imported normalization collisions fail closed; operator must reconcile, never silently merge. Production data cutover is blocked pending a workload-level equivalence audit or an explicitly approved behavior change, not just a collision-free import.

importSafety.checkpoint: SHA256/byte/count manifest per source file; complete=false on interruption. Export cannot resume an old consistent snapshot: start a new empty output directory. Converted D1 files commit a native_import_checkpoint row with data hash and count; importer resumes only identical checkpoints
importSafety.foreignKeys: Local staging preserves source constraints and validates PRAGMA foreign_key_check/integrity_check. D1 file imports may autocommit each SQL statement despite defer_foreign_keys; the sole source cycle abtest↔abtest_variable inserts abtest with nullable winner_id, inserts variables, then guardedly restores winner_id and original updated_at (ON UPDATE trigger), preserving FK enforcement and idempotent partial replay. All other FK components remain topologically ordered; final D1 counts and foreign keys are checked again.
importSafety.limits: Reject database above 10000000000 bytes, rows above 2MiB including conservative record-header allowance, SQL statements above100000 bytes, or an indivisible FK-component import file above5GiB. No data is truncated or silently omitted
importSafety.receipts: Importer writes independent per-target progress/verification receipts import-remote-<encoded-database>.json or import-local-<encoded-database>.json; production and Preview receipts never overwrite each other.
importSafety.wranglerProtocol: D1 --command reads require strict --json parsing and result-success checks. Wrangler 4.155 --file emits progress glyphs even with --json, so imports use non-JSON --yes, require exit code zero, then independently read schema/data checkpoints through strict JSON commands before accepting each file; never strip progress text into guessed JSON.
importSafety.remoteVerification: Batch destination count reads as at most 100 independent semicolon-separated SELECT statements per Wrangler --command call (not UNION ALL, which exceeds D1 compound-term limits), while checking every table. Size cap uses D1 execute response meta.size_after from a successful read-only query; unsupported table-valued pragma_page_count/page_size SQL is never issued. Failed Wrangler stdout is retained only in private importer error logs when stderr is empty.
importSafety.redis: Source Redis business data and reviewed archives are preserved losslessly except explicitly isolated external portal SSO cookies and source auth authority (sessions, reset/verification proofs and temporary registration). Excluded credentials remain only in the private source snapshot; converted manifest records key SHA-256/class/count/reason without raw values. Unknown live keyspaces still block conversion. Noncredential verification counters, pending owner-shop metadata and business keys remain mapped.
importSafety.largeRedisArchive: A native_legacy_redis payload above 32KB still respects the 2MiB row and 100KB SQL statement limits: D1 import emits an idempotent empty-row insert, bounded UTF-8-safe append statements and checked prefix/metadata/final-length guards. Converted manifest records ordered payload byte lengths and SHA-256 without raw keys; importer reads bounded payload fragments from D1 and verifies exact bytes/hash before marking import verified. Interrupted or corrupted replay fails closed; no archive record is truncated or dropped.
importSafety.springHashPaths: Spring hash fields busInfos.[N] are ordered list entries, while hourlyWeathers.[YYYYMMDDHHMM] are map properties. Consume one optional dot before a bracket index, reject empty/prototype/sparse/oversized list paths, and retain raw Redis envelopes independently; unrecognized live keys still block conversion.
importSafety.portalCredentials: KOIN_BATCH dining LOGIN_COOKIES explicitly names JSESSIONID, __KSMSID__ and KHANUSER as external portal SSO cookies cached in source Redis. User-approved separate provider/session authority excludes these exact string keys from both D1 targets; wrong types fail closed, all other unknown keys remain blocked.
importSafety.sourceSessionIsolation: Exclude refreshToken: hash, webAuthSession: string, passwordResetToken: hash, userVerificationStatus: hash, verificationStatus@: hash and StudentTemporaryStatus: hash/set (including secondary indexes) from active D1 and raw Redis archive, even when expired. These hold opaque sessions, reset/SMS proofs or temporary-registration password/authToken authority. Preserve source accounts/password hashes, owner_shop@: pending shop metadata, dailyVerifyCount@: and userDailyVerificationCount: counters, and all unrelated business rows; new prod/Preview signing keys require fresh login. Unexpected types and unknown business keys fail closed.
importSafety.reviewedUnknown: Exactly one source Redis string key of length 3 with no TTL, identified only by SHA-256 2c26b46b68ffc68ff99b453c1d30413413422d706483bfa0f98a5e886266e7ae, was user-approved for raw archive-only preservation. Producer semantics remain unknown; converted manifest records SHA-256/class/count/reason, no raw key/value. No active API/auth/batch mapping is created, and all other unrecognized live keys still fail closed.
importSafety.chat: Reconcile Mongo embedded messages and Redis zsets by decimal TSID; read/deleted flags merge monotonically, richer submillisecond timestamps survive Mongo millisecond truncation, conflicting content/identity/image values block conversion
importSafety.payment: Temporary payment import rebuilds and freezes the current cart graph, requires exact original product/total money equality, retains real PTTL, and blocks if mutable source cart no longer matches
importSafety.mongoArchive: Every original canonical Extended JSON document is also retained in native_legacy_mongo, including historical/unknown fields; no selected-column transform discards source data
importSafety.search: new_articles title bigrams backfilled using the exact domain NFC/lowercase/codepoint/stopword algorithm; ongoing title writes replace their index atomically in the community domain

ownerSmsCutover.flow: Send SMS for registration or password reset; verify six-digit code (five attempts within three minutes) to receive a random one-use verification_token. Supply phone_number and verification_token in the subsequent registration or password-reset request within three minutes. A new SMS invalidates prior proof and wrong purpose/phone/replay/expiry is rejected transactionally.
ownerSmsCutover.externalClients: The repository has no owner registration/reset HTTP consumers. External native clients using the historical OpenAPI contract must be updated for the verification_token request field and reset verification response token before switching traffic; the old JWT-shaped registration verify response is intentionally not an authentication credential.
ownerSmsCutover.safety: No unauthenticated owner registration or password reset is permitted without current SMS proof. Account and proof consumption commit in one atomic D1 batch.

previewDataCopy.source: After a final three-store source snapshot has been validated and the initial production D1 import independently verified, prepare a separately verified Preview copy from that same original snapshot; the current empty production D1 is not a data source.
previewDataCopy.isolation: Import to the distinct Preview D1 database koin-api-test (6cb9f659-47cb-4a88-99d9-1f60ca992dc9), never bind Preview to production D1 koin-api (303042db-06c1-4ddc-91c0-6bfbfd088fa4) or mutate production while preparing Preview.
previewDataCopy.privacy: User selected an unchanged copy of original member and business data, including password hashes, IDs, names, email addresses and phone numbers, into the separate Preview D1; no anonymization or derived/redacted data manifest. Import the same verified source snapshot independently into Preview. Preview must use separate signing keys, cookies, provider credentials and active session/token authority, with restricted access and no writes back to source or production; review live-provider side effects before exposing real data.
previewDataCopy.status: Planning only. MySQL-only pre-extraction marked quiesced=false/complete=false cannot be promoted to either D1 target; no Preview import or DNS/data cutover has occurred.

selectiveBatchSync.order: Complete and independently verify either the strict writer-quiesced full MySQL/Mongo/Redis snapshot or the explicitly approved per-store online full capture, then both separately targeted D1 imports before activating any recurring sync. A nonquiesced MySQL-only pre-extraction is not this initial import.
selectiveBatchSync.schedule: 0 * * * * (every hour, all day; not a five-minute or night-only schedule). The source host's cron timezone and exact installation target must be confirmed before registration.
selectiveBatchSync.scope: Only source KOIN_BATCH-owned fields/rows: dining_menus crawler fields, source lecture/semester/timetable version updates with stable destination lecture-ID reconciliation, portal article/attachment crawler fields with native hit/ownership conflict policy, and Mongo citybus_timetables. Never mirror unrelated tables or overwrite native likes, sold-out state, sessions, payments or user edits.
selectiveBatchSync.safety: Read-only source access with an approved least-privilege account, authenticated HTTPS ingestion into the independently selected D1 target, durable cursor and idempotent atomic apply, no source/production writeback from Preview, no cron activation without exact command/target/schedule approval and end-to-end verification.

fileMigration.dependency: @aws-sdk/client-s3@3.1158.0 (Node 24); explicit SDK multipart commands retain upload IDs for durable recovery
fileMigration.credentials: Runtime environment only; no credential arguments, dotenv loading or secret output. Source credential must be read-only. Cloudflare token needs read access to bucket managed/custom domains; R2 credential needs object read/write, multipart list/create/upload/complete/abort. The tool never creates public access, domains, buckets or source writes
fileMigration.privateTarget: Dedicated empty R2 bucket or matching checkpoint only. Managed r2.dev and custom domain public access are checked through the Cloudflare API before transfer and completion. Operator must independently ensure no Workers/public bindings, competing writers or lifecycle deletions, and restrict migration-data filesystem ACLs (especially on Windows). A public synthetic test bucket cannot receive source objects
fileMigration.scope: All exact current object keys and bytes, including empty objects; historical version bodies and deleted-key bodies remain in S3. Source is never deleted. No domain cutover or database URL rewriting occurs here
fileMigration.metadata: ContentType, CacheControl, ContentDisposition, ContentLanguage, ContentEncoding, Expires and complete user Metadata are copied and compared on destination reads. Private current-object JSONL preserves all readable HEAD fields, current tags and ACL. Version JSONL archives bucket versioning, every version-list entry and delete marker, including historical version IDs; unsupported ACL/tag/redirect/encryption/storage/retention semantics are audit-only, not silently mapped
fileMigration.databaseReferences: FILE_MIGRATION_DB_SNAPSHOT must be a complete exporter snapshot covering MySQL, Mongo and Redis; every manifest file hash and byte count is rechecked. Any versionId/version_id query reference found recursively in JSONL, percent-encoded strings, MySQL/Mongo binary or Redis base64 values blocks migration. FILE_MIGRATION_DB_URLS_REVIEWED confirms independent review of opaque application encodings and indirect historical-version dependencies; required historical bodies need a separately designed migration, never a bypass
fileMigration.snapshot: Two complete paginated source inventories must match before first upload. Every current object HEAD/ACL/tag record and full version/delete-marker inventory participates in SHA256 snapshot identity; final full scan must match. Additions, deletions, metadata changes and overwrites block completion. Source ETag-conditional GET additionally checks version ID, modification time, metadata and exact length. These are observational scans, not an S3 write lock: arrange an authorized stable writer window before completion/cutover
fileMigration.integrity: Hash actual source stream bytes with SHA256, durably store hash before committing object, separately GET and hash all destination bytes, and compare metadata. Never use multipart ETag as a content hash. Final target inventory checks exact count, byte totals, ETag and modification time against verified checkpoints
fileMigration.durability: Ignored repository migration-data/<FILE_MIGRATION_RUN>/ contains atomic fsynced manifest/checkpoints, baseline/observed/final current and version JSONL, and verification.jsonl with SHA256/count/byte evidence. Restart same run/environment/database snapshot only. Existing target objects need snapshot-matching checkpoints and source hashes and are re-read/rehashed; unrelated objects are never overwritten. Keep this private audit directory backed up
fileMigration.failureRecovery: Transfer failure aborts its unfinished multipart upload. Restart aborts only exact checkpoint-owned upload IDs and restarts that object; completed verified objects are rehashed, not overwritten. A hard kill between remote creation and local upload-ID persistence leaves an unknown upload and fails closed for manual ownership reconciliation. run.lock is exclusive: after a hard kill, verify the original process is dead before manually removing only that local lock. Never discard checkpoints or clear a target bucket to force a resume
fileMigration.limits: Single-object sequential streaming with one dynamically sized multipart buffer (8 MiB minimum, up to 524 MiB at R2 maximum), at most 10000 parts. R2 maximum supported size is 5 TiB minus 5 GiB; larger objects fail before upload. Archive-tier unreadable objects and unavailable source ACL/tag/version permissions fail closed; the tool does not restore or modify source objects. Multipart completion sends If-None-Match plus a pre-completion existence check, but exclusive target-writer access remains required because R2 documentation does not promise conditional multipart completion
